source: WHO Clinical Guidelines / BTS Pleural Disease Guidelines 2023
description: Abnormal accumulation of fluid in the pleural space, visible on chest X-ray as meniscus sign or opacification

criteria: Small effusion: blunting of costophrenic angle only
mild.label: Small pleural effusion — investigate cause

criteria: Moderate effusion: fluid level above diaphragm, partial lung opacification
moderate.label: Moderate pleural effusion — treat and consider drainage

criteria: Large effusion: near-complete or complete opacification of hemithorax
severe.label: Large pleural effusion — urgent drainage

actions: If suspected TB: sputum testing, start TB workup
Fluid analysis: protein, LDH, cell count, gram stain, AFB, cytology
Light's criteria to differentiate transudate vs exudate

tuberculosis.note: Start standard TB regimen (2HRZE/4HR) if TB confirmed

actions: Urgent therapeutic thoracentesis or chest tube drainage
Do not drain >1500ml in first session (risk of re-expansion pulmonary edema)
Refer to specialist for chest tube / pleurodesis if needed

within_1_week: Need for diagnostic thoracentesis not available locally
